text:
Maria: Quick heads-up — I ran a cross-device autotune sweep (L4/T4/A10 vs A100/H100) against the new preset-scheduler and hit a weird latency bump on L4 at seqlen=128. p95 jumped ~18% vs previous preset. stack traces look KV-cache heavy. Anyone seen this pattern?

Kevin: hmm, did you lock batching config? autotune might pick a cheaper kernel that inflates KV copy costs on small-memory GPUs. :thinking:

Maria: Batching fixed (max_batch=8, burst=16). I think it's the kernel pick: the autotuner switched from Winograd-ish matmul -> int8-fused kernel for L4 at that seqlen. On A100/H100 we stayed on the float16/fft path.

Sam: Can you paste the autotune decisions and the runtime profile? tiny logs help.

Maria: pasted below — it's a single-thread run to isolate behavior.

```
# autotune decisions (relevant lines)
device L4: kernel=INT8_FUSED_MATMUL preset=hetero-smallmem seqlen=128 latency_est=3.2ms
device A100: kernel=FUSED_FWD_FP16 preset=perf-default seqlen=128 latency_est=2.1ms

# perf snapshot (mini-run)
p50: L4=5.1ms, A100=2.7ms
p95: L4=12.6ms, A100=3.2ms
kv-copy-time L4: 6.3ms (spike)
```

Olivia: That KV-copy-time looks huge — could be pinned memory fallback or an memcpy path from device->host->device. Does the L4 ioctl path support the same pinned alloc as A100?

Kevin: L4 drivers we use sometimes fall back to non-GPU pinned pages for small-ish allocations. If the kernel uses a tiled KV layout that increases memcpy count, you'll see this. Try forcing pinned_alloc=true in the runtime for L4 and re-run.

Maria: Good call. Re-ran with pinned_alloc=true and also forced kernel to FUSED_FWD_FP16 for L4. Results: p95 back down to ~3.5ms. autotune still prefers INT8_FUSED when allowed.

perf-bot: perf-summary: run=2165432142 devices=[L4] preset=hetero-smallmem seqlen=128 autotune_pick=INT8_FUSED_MATMUL p95_delta=+17.9% kv_copy_ms=6.27 suggested_action=try_pinned_alloc or tune_kernel_cost_fn

Jordan: Looks like a modeling issue in the autotuner cost function — it underweights memcpy/KV overhead for small GPU memory architectures. We should add a device-memory-bandwidth factor and an explicit KV-copy penalty for kernels that require extra staging.

Sam: Agreed. For immediate mitigation we can add a per-device override table: prefer FP16 path for L4/T4/A10 at seqlen >= 64 when KV working set > X. Longer term we should surface the memcpy cost in the profiling harness so autotune learns it.

Olivia: I can add a quick smoke test to eng-runtime/perf-harness that floods KV cache and measures copy path. Want it gated behind a flag.

Maria: Please do. For now I'll push a small preset change: hetero-smallmem v2 that prefers FP16 at seqlen>=64 and toggles pinned_alloc by default on L4/T4. Will roll to staging. :thumbsup:

Kevin: ping me once it's in staging — I'll run the regression matrix across A10 too.

Maria: thanks all — saving logs and flamegraph in the ticket: https://redwood.fake/tickets/INF-8421 — include that when you run reproducer.

Jordan: Filing a follow-up issue to update autotuner: INF-8422 (add memcpy penalty + device memory bandwidth term).

Maria: Cool. We'll monitor canary. If anyone wants the reproducer: run `./tools/run_repro.sh --device L4 --seqlen 128 --preset hetero-smallmem` and see p95 jump. Repro env: runtime v2.9.1, kernellib 1.14, driver 525.

Sam: Nice repro, thanks. I'll try a quick microbenchmark to estimate memcpy ratio and open a PR with the harness change.

perf-bot: note: reaction :eyes: on Maria's last message

Maria: closing thread for now — will post results after staging canary. :wave:
